public_payload.normalized_proposition: Claude is not very good at mass domestic surveillance and cannot run fully autonomous weapons at all.

statement.excerpt: The Department of Defense had agreed to terms around not using Claude for mass domestic surveillance or fully autonomous killing machines (the former of which it’s not particularly good at and the latter of which it flat out cannot do)
statement.document_title: The AI Bubble Is An Information War

our_interpretation: Following the supplied normalized proposition, this assessment concerns Claude's capabilities, not whether the Pentagon accepted contractual restrictions.

The ordinary reading is that contemporary Claude performs poorly at large-scale analysis of Americans' personal data and cannot operate a weapon that selects and engages targets without human approval.
Not particularly good implies poor practical accuracy or usefulness, without supplying a numerical threshold.

The target is the latest publicly describable capability state during the late-February negotiations through publication. Later models or later demonstrations cannot establish that earlier state without a documented connection.
criteria.support_condition: Representative evaluations show poor practical surveillance performance, and technical evidence establishes inability to perform autonomous target selection and engagement in the relevant configuration.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Representative evaluations demonstrate useful surveillance performance, or a documented contemporary system using Claude successfully performs autonomous target selection and engagement.
